These data are consistent with a causal association between elevated lipoprotein(a) levels and increased risk of MI.

Observational hazard ratios for aortic valve stenosis and MI were similar after further adjustment for CRP levels. Elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) were not causally associated with increased low-grade inflammation as measured through CRP despite a causal association with increased risk of aortic valve stenosis and MI.
